findings.title: The resolver and the mod can't find the engine from the Bash tool or without a plugin root
findings.claim: The resolver's cache step reads $CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA and its dev-checkout step reads $CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT. The Phase 1 research measured both as unset in the Bash tool. Skills (and the curator agent) reach the engine only through Bash. The mod's first call is `ROOT + "/scripts/planroom"`, but no verified mod API supplies ROOT, and no [A] entry covers it. On a cached (git or GitHub marketplace) install, the skill path therefore has no cache location and no dev checkout, and the mod path is unspecified.
findings.evidence: architecture.md §Packaging and release (line 1205): the order is "$PLANROOM_ENGINE, then the dev checkout ($CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT/../target/...), then the cache in $CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA, then a sha256-verified download". architecture.md §Skills (1107) says skills run `"${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/planroom"` via body substitution. architecture.md §Wiring (1060) uses `ROOT + "/scripts/planroom"`. plugin-packaging.md §3, Bash tool environment [verified]: "R=unset D=unset  # CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT/DATA not in Bash env". plugin-packaging.md §Design implications step 3 says that when DATA is unset, fall back to $PLANROOM_DATA (passed by skills) or XDG; DR-28 and the architecture dropped that step. mod-api.md §7 lists $.session.root (the session's root), $.env.get with literal names, and nothing for the plugin's own directory. The C4 container diagram (line 132) has the curator running "Bash: planroom curate", but there is no bin/, so `planroom` is not on PATH. KICKOFF S14.3: "an agent can drive S1 and S2 using only the plugin's tools and skills".
findings.failure_scenario: A user runs `/plugin marketplace add doodla/planroom`, then installs. The plugin is copied into ~/.claude/plugins/cache/..., so ../target doesn't exist. The model loads the `room` skill and runs `"/home/u/.claude/plugins/cache/planroom/planroom/0.1.0/scripts/planroom" find worker --json` through Bash. CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA is empty, so the cache lookup resolves to `/engine/0.1.0/planroom` and misses. The download then tries to write under `/engine` (EACCES), or it re-downloads into an ad-hoc directory on every call. The mod meanwhile cached the engine under ~/.claude/plugins/data/planroom-planroom, a location the skill path never sees. S14.3's skill path fails or re-downloads per command, and the curator agent can't run `planroom curate` at all (S12 evidence).
findings.proposed_fix: Make the resolver depend on nothing in its environment except optional overrides. Locate engine.env and the dev checkout from the script's own path (`$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)`), not from $CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT. Use one data root: `${PLANROOM_DATA:-${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA:-${XDG_DATA_HOME:-$HOME/.local/share}/planroom}}`. Better still, always use the XDG path, so the mod, the Bash tool and agents share one cache, and prune old versions on each successful resolve. Add an assumption A-12 to spike in WS8: how the mod learns its plugin root (`import.meta.url`, `$.env.get('CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT')`, or a generated constant), and whether `$.process.run` children inherit HTTPS_PROXY. Have the mod pass the resolved absolute engine path to spawned agents in their prompt or env. Have the curator agent call the resolver path. Add an installer-suite case that runs the resolver under `env -i HOME=... PATH=...` with no CLAUDE_* variables.

findings.title: Canvas assets sit at `<exe dir>/canvas/`, which the dev build and the cargo-install fallback never create
findings.claim: `serve` (and `share`, which builds its Artifact fragment from the Vite index.html) look for the built canvas next to the executable. The canvas is built to target/canvas/, while the binary is at target/release/planroom or target/debug/planroom. The KICKOFF fallback `cargo install --git` installs only the binary into ~/.cargo/bin, with no canvas, and a cargo build can't produce one. Only the release archive puts canvas/ beside the binary.
findings.evidence: architecture.md §Local server (1047) and contracts.md:254: "the canvas build, from `<exe dir>/canvas/`". repo-layout.md:53: "canvas ... builds to target/canvas/". repo-layout.md:190: `target/canvas/` comes from `cargo xtask gen --canvas`. architecture.md:1205: fallback `cargo install --locked --git ... planroom`. The design embeds packs (`crates/planroom/build.rs`) but not the canvas. KICKOFF constraints: "the local server serves the canvas's built assets"; "The fallback is `cargo install --git` or a local build". S14: "From a fresh clone, the release build (`cargo build --release` plus the frontend build) runs on the built fixture". WS5 and WS6 load the plugin "with the engine built from source" (the dev-checkout path).
findings.failure_scenario: Walking skeleton WS6, or the S14 evidence run: the person clones, runs `cargo build --release` and `cargo xtask gen --canvas`, installs the local marketplace, and presses `e` in the pane. The resolver picks target/release/planroom, and `serve` looks in target/release/canvas/, which doesn't exist. The browser gets a 404 or a blank page, which also breaks the "no blank state" principle. `/room share` can't find index.html, so S11 has no page. A user who lands on the fallback (no matching release asset) gets the CLI and mod but never a canvas.
findings.proposed_fix: Embed the built canvas in the binary (rust-embed or include_dir) from a build.rs that reads `target/canvas/` when it is present. When it is absent, serve one engine-rendered page that names the fix (`cargo xtask gen --canvas`) and returns the `empty.next` envelope, so neither `serve` nor `share` depends on file layout. If embedding is rejected, search `$PLANROOM_CANVAS_DIR`, then `<exe dir>/canvas`, then `<exe dir>/../canvas`, and have the resolver's fallback also fetch a `planroom-canvas-vVERSION.tar.gz` asset. Add a smoke step to `tests/plugin/install.sh` and `release-dry-run` that runs `serve` from target/release/ and from a `cargo install --path` root, and fetches `/`.

findings.title: The source-build fallback is pinned to a tag that can't exist during the build or before the owner releases, and the 'build from source' card is unspecified
findings.claim: Every non-dev fallback is `cargo install --git ... --tag vVERSION`, and the download is for the fixed tag vVERSION. KICKOFF forbids the agent to push tags, so during the whole build, and whenever main carries a version the owner hasn't released yet, both the asset fetch and the fallback fail. The mod's card "Build the engine from source, about 4 minutes?" doesn't say which command it runs. It doesn't say what process it runs in: `process.spawn` children die on reload and session end, and `process.run` caps at 10 minutes. It doesn't say what it checks first (cargo present, Rust at or above the pinned 1.97, Node and pnpm for the canvas). It doesn't say how an interrupted fetch's lock and partial download are recovered.
findings.evidence: architecture.md:1205 and DR-28 ("then prints the exact cargo install fallback"; the mod deals the card). KICKOFF:274: "Don't, without me: ... push tags, create GitHub releases". KICKOFF:236: "The fallback is `cargo install --git` or a local build." KICKOFF S14.2: "Test the source-build path live". mod-api.md §7: process.run has "a 10 min maximum"; process.spawn "dies on every hot reload and at session end". repo-layout.md:212: Rust pinned to 1.97.0 in rust-toolchain.toml, which `cargo install --git` doesn't honour (rustup reads the invoking directory). plugin-packaging.md §Design implications: a `mkdir` lock between the prefetch and the run. feature_list S14 tests "a concurrent prefetch and run" but not a killed one. iris-release-bar §3: Iris cuts a release by bumping on a branch and merging to main before tagging, which opens a window.
findings.failure_scenario: S14 evidence, in a fresh session on a machine without a prebuilt target/: no v0.1.0 release exists, so the download returns 404. The card runs `cargo install --tag v0.1.0` and fails with "tag not found", so the live source-build path KICKOFF asks for can't pass. Later, the owner merges a 0.2.0 bump to main and tags it a day after. Everyone who installs or updates in between gets a 404 and a failing card. Separately, a person quits Claude Code during the first-run download. The spawned prefetch dies holding the mkdir lock, and the next session's resolver waits on or refuses the stale lock, so every surface shows "Getting the Planroom engine..." indefinitely.
findings.proposed_fix: When the plugin is loaded from a checkout (script path/../Cargo.toml exists), the card runs `cargo build --release --locked -p planroom` there, then `cargo xtask gen --canvas` (or relies on the embedded canvas, see operability-2). Only for cached installs does it run `cargo install --locked --git URL --tag vVERSION`. When `git ls-remote` shows no such tag, it says so plainly and offers `--branch main` with an explicit warning that the version won't match. Before dealing the card, preflight `cargo --version` against `rust-version`, and node/pnpm if the canvas isn't embedded, and name the exact missing tool. Run the build as a detached, logged child (`setsid`, log in the data directory, pid file), so a reload doesn't kill it, and have the status line tail the log. Make the lock stale-safe: write a pid and timestamp inside the lock dir, and break the lock if `kill -0` fails or it is older than 15 minutes. Add `tests/installer` cases for a killed prefetch and a missing tag. In releasing.md, order the release so main never names an unpublished version: tag the release commit and publish, then fast-forward main.

findings.title: Store migrations run in place with no automatic backup, and the store is the only copy of everything a person authored
findings.claim: Any newer binary that opens an older store migrates it in place. All user-authored state (plans, overrides, reviews, decisions, the ledger) lives only in WORKSPACE/.planroom/store.db. That directory is gitignored, there is no per-repo export [DR-34], and backup is a manual `planroom export`. A bad migration, a crash mid-migration on a non-transactional DDL step, or a plugin rollback afterwards leaves the person with no recoverable copy: older binaries refuse a newer store with `schema_mismatch`.
findings.evidence: contracts.md §Store schema and migrations (279): "One that finds an older one migrates after asking any older serve to drain". architecture.md:457: "`planroom export` ... the escape hatch for upgrades and backups" (manual). architecture.md:463: `.planroom/` has "a .gitignore of *". DR-34: "the workspace store is the one source". architecture.md §Security, Store integrity: "`export` for backups". KICKOFF principles: "Never lose or overwrite what someone did"; "Everything is reversible, which is what makes bold defaults safe". KICKOFF stance: "migrations, upgrades" are gaps the owner must handle.
findings.failure_scenario: The user updates the plugin to 0.2.0, and an agent's first `planroom find` migrates the store. A bug in migration 0004 rewrites `events.body` wrongly; the fixture test only covered the previous release's fixture, not this user's data shape. The fold now errors or drops overrides. The user reinstalls 0.1.0 to recover, and it refuses the store with `schema_mismatch`. No pre-migration copy exists, so weeks of plans and corrections are gone, which breaks both principles.
findings.proposed_fix: Before any migration, the engine writes `VACUUM INTO '.planroom/backups/store-v{old}-{utc}.db'` (or uses the SQLite online-backup API), checks that `PRAGMA integrity_check` and a fold of the copy succeed, and keeps the last 3 backups. It runs every migration plus a post-migration fold in one `BEGIN EXCLUSIVE` transaction and rolls back on any fold error. It emits a warning code `store_migrated` with the backup path in `meta.warnings`, so the mod shows one line. Add `planroom doctor --restore BACKUP` (or document `import` of an export written by the backup) as the downgrade path. Tests: migrate a fixture, corrupt the migration on purpose, and assert that the original store and the backup are intact.

findings.title: Version skew between sessions, a reused older `serve`, and the dev checkout is handled only during migrations
findings.claim: The handshake drains an older `serve` only before a migration. In every other case `serve --detach` is idempotent through serve.json, so a newer mod reuses an older running server and gets its old canvas and API. After another session migrates the store, an older session's mod restarts `watch` through its own, older resolver. That resolver picks the same older engine, which exits with `schema_mismatch` again, so the session loops without telling the person to reload. The dev-checkout step accepts target/release before target/debug whenever the crate version matches, and that version doesn't change between commits, so a stale binary is preferred over a fresh one. No check compares the mod's generated catalogue with the engine's.
findings.evidence: architecture.md:1052, Version handshake: drain "before migrating the store"; "the mod restarts `watch` through the resolver". architecture.md:153: serve is "idempotent through .planroom/serve.json". architecture.md:1205: "`$CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT/../target/{release,debug}/planroom` when its version matches". mod-api.md §7: $.state is session-scoped. R10 (several Claude sessions at once) makes mixed plugin versions across open sessions normal after an update.
findings.failure_scenario: The user has three sessions open and updates the plugin in one. It migrates the store. The other two sessions' watch loops spin on `schema_mismatch`, every pane action errors, and the person isn't told to run /reload-plugins. In development, a release build from yesterday shadows today's debug build. The committed mod bundle sends a command the stale engine doesn't know, and S9 evidence runs against mismatched code.
findings.proposed_fix: Have `planroom version --json` report `{version, git_commit, schema_version, catalogue_hash}`. The mod compares catalogue_hash with its generated constant and, on a mismatch, shows one card or status line ("Planroom engine X doesn't match this plugin; reload"). Make `serve --detach` drain any serve whose version or catalogue_hash differs from its own, not just before migrations. On `schema_mismatch` with `found > supported`, the mod stops restarting `watch` and shows "Updated in another session: /reload-plugins". The dev-checkout step picks the newest of release and debug by mtime and requires a matching git_commit or catalogue_hash. The outbox survives as long as $.state does.

findings.title: The release workflow is a one-line sketch below the Iris bar, and the macOS x86_64 and musl build details are unrecorded
findings.claim: release.yml is described only as "runs on a v* tag push or workflow_dispatch; only publish has contents: write". It lacks the gates Iris has: a `verify` job (tag equals the version in Cargo, plugin.json, package.json and engine.env; the CHANGELOG section exists and is non-empty; notes extracted), `checks` re-run on the tagged commit, and a publish step that fails unless exactly the four expected archives plus SHA256SUMS are present. Both darwin targets build on arm64 macos-15. The x86_64-apple-darwin smoke test then runs an x86_64 binary on an arm64 runner (Rosetta), while Iris uses macos-15-intel. The musl C-toolchain settings that the rusqlite bundle and the tree-sitter grammars need (musl-tools, `CC_aarch64_unknown_linux_musl=musl-gcc`) aren't recorded.
findings.evidence: repo-layout.md §CI workflows (265-267). architecture.md:1206. iris-release-bar.md §3: Triggers and gating (verify, checks, publish asserts "exactly the four expected names"); Targets table (`x86_64-apple-darwin` on `macos-15-intel`; `CC_aarch64_unknown_linux_musl=musl-gcc`). KICKOFF R15 and the release-bar constraint: "Match doodla/iris ... a release workflow". KICKOFF S14: "CI is green on the pushed branch", and the release-dry-run matrix runs on every push.
findings.failure_scenario: The owner pushes v0.1.0 on a commit whose plugin.json still says 0.0.9. The release publishes assets named for 0.1.0, while installed plugins request 0.0.9 and get a 404. Or the x86_64-darwin smoke step fails on every branch push because the arm64 runner can't execute x86_64 binaries, which turns S14's 'CI green' red, or it is silently skipped and an untested binary ships.
findings.proposed_fix: Specify release.yml as Iris's verify → checks → build(matrix) → publish. Have `scripts/check-tag-version.sh` also compare plugin.json, every package.json and engine.env. Add a changelog-section gate, and an exact asset-set check before `gh release create`. Use `macos-15-intel` for x86_64-apple-darwin, or install Rosetta explicitly in that job and record why. Record the musl CC and C++ settings in the release table, and a DR if anything departs from Iris.

findings.title: The breaking-change guard compares with origin/main's tip, and CI's shallow clone can't run the git-history checks
findings.claim: `cargo xtask check` compares the generated schema with `origin/main`. On a branch, the tip of main moves underneath it, so a branch that didn't touch the schema can 'remove' a property main gained after it branched. The result then depends on when origin/main was last fetched, which isn't deterministic. `actions/checkout` defaults to fetch-depth 1 with no origin/main, and `xtask eval --verify-order` ("check label order with git") needs history. Neither is provided for in the CI description.
findings.evidence: contracts.md §Versioning rules (16): "compares the generated schema with origin/main and fails on a removed property...". repo-layout.md:200: `eval --verify-order` "check label order with git". repo-layout.md:255: CI sets `persist-credentials: false`, and no fetch depth is stated. KICKOFF: "deterministic commands"; "One task entry point runs the same check ... locally and in CI"; S14 "CI is green on the pushed branch".
findings.failure_scenario: Track A merges a new `PaneModel.drift_count` to main. The main agent's branch, based earlier, pushes. In CI, `check` reports "removed property drift_count without a schema_version bump" and goes red, though the branch never touched it. Locally the same command passes because origin/main is stale. On the very first push, the shallow checkout has no origin/main and `--verify-order` can't walk the label history, so both checks error.
findings.proposed_fix: Compare against the schema at `git merge-base HEAD origin/main`. Once a release exists, also compare against the last released tag's schema (the compatibility users actually rely on), and pass with a 'skipped (no base)' line when no base exists. In ci.yml, check out with `fetch-depth: 0` (or explicitly `git fetch --no-tags origin main` plus the label commits) for the `check` and `test` jobs, and document both in repo-layout.md.

findings.title: First run when mods are off, or the mod consent is declined, is undesigned
findings.claim: Every surface the plugin advertises (`/room`, the three tools, the pane, the prefetch, the engine card) lives in the mod. Mods need a one-time 'turn on mods' consent. The design says nothing about a fresh install where that consent hasn't been given or is refused: whether the skills still work through Bash, what the person sees, or what the README says.
findings.evidence: KICKOFF verified facts: "The first mod file you write triggers a one-time 'turn on mods' question"; KICKOFF S14.3: "`/room` works". grep finds no mention of mod consent or mods-off behaviour in architecture.md, decisions.md or repo-layout.md. KICKOFF principle: "Never show a blank state."
findings.failure_scenario: A new user installs planroom@planroom with mods disabled. No `/room` exists, no tools are listed, and nothing explains why. The model may still load the hidden `room` skill and hit the resolver, which hits the problems in operability-1 with no prefetch having run.
findings.proposed_fix: State the degraded mode: skills plus the resolver work with mods off, the resolver fetches on first call, and plugin/README.md plus the `room` skill say in one line that the pane and /room need mods turned on, and how. Add an install-suite assertion that, with the mod disabled, the skill path resolves the engine and `focus --json` returns a non-empty envelope.

findings.title: No owner runbook: the clicks, repo settings and release order KICKOFF requires aren't prepared
findings.claim: The design defers tagging and releases to the owner but never lists the owner's steps. These include the release order (see operability-3), tag and push, and running Release. They also include repo settings the design depends on: uploading the 1280×640 social preview (a Settings-only action), enabling private vulnerability reporting (which SECURITY.md will point to, per Iris), and enabling Dependabot alerts and security updates. releasing.md is only named as a future doc.
findings.evidence: architecture.md:1207: "Tagging, creating the GitHub release and any registry publishing stay with the owner". architecture.md:1302: the social preview art. iris-release-bar.md §1 #5: SECURITY.md uses "Private reporting through GitHub's Security tab". KICKOFF:274: "Prepare them, and list exactly what I need to click"; KICKOFF:230: the final message lists "the exact clicks I owe (tag, release, any registry names or tokens, repo settings)".
findings.failure_scenario: At the end of the build the final message lists 'tag v0.1.0'. The owner tags before the version bump reaches main, or without uploading the social preview or enabling private reporting. SECURITY.md then points to a disabled button, and the social card shows GitHub's default.
findings.proposed_fix: Add an 'Owner checklist' section to docs/contributing/releasing.md and make a docs test assert it exists. It lists, in order: merge the branch; confirm CI is green on main; run Release as a dry run; `git tag vX.Y.Z <sha> && git push origin vX.Y.Z`; check the release assets; Settings → Social preview upload (path to the PNG); Settings → Security → enable private vulnerability reporting and Dependabot alerts and security updates. Generate the final message's click list from it.

findings.title: Dependabot npm PRs will be red against pnpm's 7-day minimumReleaseAge
findings.claim: pnpm refuses versions younger than 7 days, while Dependabot opens weekly PRs for the newest versions, often hours old. CI runs on pushes to every branch, Dependabot's included, so those branches go red by construction and add noise. Nothing aligns the two.
findings.evidence: repo-layout.md:217: `minimumReleaseAge: 10080`. repo-layout.md:29: dependabot.yml for "cargo, npm, github-actions; weekly, grouped". repo-layout.md:255: `push` to `branches: ["**"]`. architecture.md §Security, Supply chain: the same pnpm setting.
findings.failure_scenario: Every Monday Dependabot pushes `dependabot/npm_and_yarn/...`. `pnpm install` fails on a package published 2 days earlier, so CI is red on that branch. The owner learns to ignore red Dependabot runs, which hides real advisories.
findings.proposed_fix: Set `cooldown: { default-days: 7 }` in dependabot.yml for the npm ecosystem (and for cargo and actions, for consistency). Add a `release_pins`-style test that the cooldown equals minimumReleaseAge/1440.

findings.title: Wall-clock CI gates run on shared runners, macOS included, with no-retry rules
findings.claim: The per-push CI gates on several latencies: cold scan under 5 s, fold under 50 ms via `cargo bench`, commit-to-stream p99 under 1 s (S8 in `test (os)` on macos-15 as well), and five of five canvas loads under 1 s with no retry for slowness. Shared runners, especially macOS, have noisy neighbours, so a tier A requirement (CI green, S14) is exposed to flakes unrelated to the change.
findings.evidence: architecture.md §Performance budgets (1171-1183): "CI gate" on each. DR-43: "never because it was slow". repo-layout.md:262: `test (os)` on ubuntu-24.04 and macos-15. ts-stack measurements cited in DR-43: 1.4 to 1.6 s at 4× throttling.
findings.failure_scenario: A docs-only push fails because a macos-15 runner's p99 commit-to-stream hit 1.2 s under I/O contention with `synchronous = FULL`. The branch is red, S14's 'CI green on the pushed branch' fails at the final push, and the agent burns a cycle rerunning.
findings.proposed_fix: Keep the thresholds. Run the timing assertions in one dedicated job on ubuntu-24.04 that records every sample in the job summary. On macOS, assert S8's functional invariants and record (but don't gate) latency, and say so in DR-43 (KICKOFF requires no macOS gate). Express the fold bench as an instruction-count or iteration-count budget (for example, criterion with a fixed iteration count compared against a committed baseline with a margin) instead of an absolute 50 ms.

findings.title: Several CI-path tools rest on unverified behaviour: `plugin details` counting mod tools, browser install, and the Claude Code install
findings.claim: `surface_tokens.sh` reads always-on cost from `claude plugin details`. Research saw `details` count skills, agents and MCP servers, but the tools are registered at runtime by the mod (`$.tool.register`), and nothing shows `details` counts them, so the 1,500-token gate may pass vacuously. The Playwright pin is said to match "the preinstalled browsers", which exist only in this container: GitHub runners need an explicit `playwright install chromium`. CI "installs" Claude Code 2.1.310 with no source, no checksum and auto-update left on, though the supply-chain row says CI tools are sha256-pinned.
findings.evidence: architecture.md:845 and DR-22: the gate is "read from `claude plugin details`". plugin-packaging.md §1: the `details` output lists "Skills · Agents · Hooks · MCP servers · Always-on ~67 tok", with no mod tools. repo-layout.md:219-221: "Playwright 1.63.0 ... matches the preinstalled browsers"; "Claude Code 2.1.310 | an xtask constant, which CI installs". architecture.md §Security, Supply chain: "CI tools downloaded with pinned sha256".
findings.failure_scenario: A change doubles the `room_query` description. `details` reports only the skill frontmatter, the gate stays green, and every session pays the extra tokens. Or the first CI e2e run fails with 'Executable doesn't exist at ~/.cache/ms-playwright/chromium-...'. Or Claude Code auto-updates mid-job, and `plugin validate` behaviour changes under a pinned test.
findings.proposed_fix: Verify in WS8 whether `claude plugin details` includes mod-registered tools. If it doesn't, compute the projection from the generated TOOL_SPECS plus the skill frontmatter plus the prompt section in xtask, and cross-check it once against the live `init` event on the evidence path. Have `cargo xtask e2e` run `playwright install chromium` (with `--with-deps` on CI) at the pinned version. Install Claude Code through a sha256-pinned artifact with `DISABLE_AUTOUPDATER=1`, and add that to the release_pins table.

verdicts.reason: The architecture resolver reads the dev checkout from $CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT and the cache from $CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA. Research verified that neither is set in the Bash tool. Skill bodies substitute only the script path, not the env inside the script. Research suggested a PLANROOM_DATA/XDG fallback, and DR-28 and the architecture dropped it. No mod API gives ROOT. Even on S14's local-path install, a skill invocation expands $CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT/../target to /../target inside the script and misses. It then falls through to a download of a tag that doesn't exist yet. S14.3 is tier A, so this is material.
verdicts.evidence: architecture.md:1205 gives the order "$PLANROOM_ENGINE, then the dev checkout ($CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT/../target/...), then the cache in $CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA". plugin-packaging.md:133 records "R=unset D=unset # CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT/DATA not in Bash env". plugin-packaging.md:239 has the PLANROOM_DATA/XDG fallback, which is absent from decisions.md:494. architecture.md:1060 uses `ROOT + "/scripts/planroom"`. mod-api.md:310 lists $.session.root and $.env.get (literal names) and nothing for the plugin directory. No A-NN entry covers it (architecture.md:1330-1340).

verdicts.reason: serve takes the canvas from `<exe dir>/canvas/`, while the build writes it to target/canvas/ and the binary sits in target/{release,debug}/. Nothing embeds or copies the canvas: only packs are embedded via build.rs. Neither `cargo install --git` nor a local build produces <exe dir>/canvas. The dev-checkout path used by the walking skeleton and the S14 'fresh clone, release build runs' step would serve 404s. share's index.html is affected the same way. Only the release archive layout works.
verdicts.evidence: architecture.md:1047 and contracts.md:254 say "the canvas build, from `<exe dir>/canvas/`". repo-layout.md:53 says "builds to target/canvas/", and repo-layout.md:190 says target/canvas/ comes from `cargo xtask gen --canvas`. architecture.md:503 embeds only packs. A grep for embed/include_dir/PLANROOM_CANVAS found no canvas embedding. KICKOFF:236 says "The fallback is `cargo install --git` or a local build".

verdicts.reason: Both the asset download and the cargo fallback are pinned to tag vVERSION. KICKOFF forbids the agent from pushing tags, so neither can succeed before the owner releases. Yet S14.2 requires the source-build path to be tested live, and in a fresh clone with no target/ the mod card's build has nothing to run. The card's command, process model (spawn dies on reload, run caps at 10 min), preflight and stale-lock recovery are unspecified. The feature list tests only a concurrent prefetch, not a killed one.

verdicts.reason: Migrations run in place automatically when a newer binary opens an older store. The only backup is a manual `planroom export`. The store is the single source of authored state and is gitignored, and older binaries refuse a migrated store. A buggy migration on real user data therefore loses work, which is a data-loss risk under the materiality definition and conflicts with 'Never lose or overwrite what someone did'. One nuance: SQLite DDL is transactional, so the 'non-transactional DDL' sub-claim is weak. But the design never says migrations plus a verify fold run in one transaction, and it has no pre-migration copy.
